reason: Attacked on translation drift and could not break it. I downloaded the OCR of the Loeb scan the March verifier used (archive.org in.ernet.dli.2015.98705, the Heinemann and Harvard Odes and Epodes with Bennett's translation). Under Ode XXX, The Poet's Immortal Fame, it reads: I HAVE finished a monument more lasting than bronze and loftier than the Pyramids’ royal pile, one that no wasting rain, no furious north wind can destroy, or the countless chain of years and the ages’ flight. I shall not altogether die. That is word for word the card, with the small capitals lowered and curly apostrophes kept. The March refuter checked the 1914 first printing by Google Books search-inside (hog_AQAAMAAJ), which puts it on p. 279, and the 1921 printing agrees, so the p. 279 now in the source is supported. Lines 1 to 5 is right: the Latin sentence ends at fuga temporum in line 5 and Non omnis moriar opens line 6. Bennett is prose, so the quotation is rightly unbroken, and Poetry is the form of the work. The CFL wording (I have raised a monument) is another rendering and is correctly not used. shipped.js: not shipped, no near match, Horace at 1 of 3 (March), not banned. Not on the misattribution list. The source line leads with the name, has no dash and runs 105 characters. The line is publishable and on theme: the work that outlasts its maker. Editor's note, not a refutation: this is the same text as carry-in 03-cfl-08, so land one of the two, not both.
